name: Whimsical
tagline: Fast collaborative flowcharts, wireframes, mind maps, and docs

pricing.notes: Official pricing/help checked 2026-07-30; Pro listed at $12/editor/month monthly and $10/editor/month annually.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited private boards and members; 3 team boards, 3 teams, 10 guests, 5MB/file, 1GB storage, 7-day history, 20 AI credits/workspace total
tiers.notes: Maximum 2 free workspaces; viewers are always free.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited team boards; 6 teams, 50 guests, 1GB/file, 100GB storage and 90-day history

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited teams; starting at 200 guests, 10GB/file, starting at 2TB storage, unlimited history, SAML SSO and SCIM
tiers.notes: $240/editor/year when billed annually; custom terms/invoicing available through sales.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited private boards and workspace members; 3 collaborative team boards, 3 teams, 10 guests, 2 free workspaces, 5MB/file, 1GB storage, 7-day history and 20 AI credits/workspace total
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every editor is charged separately in each upgraded workspace; viewers are free. Additional AI credits are sold but their price is not public. Adding/removing editors creates prorated charges/credits; custom legal/security terms require sales.

verdictSummary: A constrained diagramming tool with nodes, connectors, sticky notes, and export is a very vibecodable core loop; polish and collaboration are what you lose.
coreLoopDIY: Create a canvas with node shapes, connectors, auto-layout hints, text editing, and PNG/SVG export.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for speed and tidy diagrams that teammates can edit without setup.

priorArt.name: Excalidraw
priorArt.desc: Open-source virtual whiteboard with diagramming, shapes, collaboration options, and export

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Docs, whiteboards, databases, mind maps, tasks, and presentation frames in one finished app; the free hosted limits are tolerable for one person or a tiny team.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.engines: Self-hosted AFFiNE AI can be configured with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and FAL credentials
facts.dataFormat: Local-first clients keep workspace data locally and sync to AFFiNE Cloud or the operator's server; self-hosting uses PostgreSQL, Redis, and persistent blob storage
facts.gapVsPaid: AFFiNE's diagram and wireframe libraries, keyboard-driven speed, and visual refinement are less mature than Whimsical's focused collaborative editor.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted/desktop app installs cleanly; self-hosting is a multi-service Docker deployment that needs a domain, TLS, secrets, storage, backups, and AI-provider keys for AI features

alternatives.name: CryptPad
alternatives.desc: Private collaborative docs, whiteboards, diagrams, slides, and Kanban in one suite; rougher edges, fewer tasteful shortcuts, and no native mind-map mode.

facts.install: Use a public CryptPad instance, or self-host the Node.js service behind a reverse proxy
facts.dataFormat: Documents are encrypted in the browser before upload; the server stores encrypted document files, blobs, and account pin metadata on its filesystem and cannot read document content
facts.gapVsPaid: CryptPad lacks native mind maps and polished wireframe components, and its diagramming and document experience is considerably rougher than Whimsical.
facts.setupBlocker: Public hosting is immediate; self-hosting requires two domains or subdomains, HTTPS, strict security headers, Node.js configuration, persistent storage, and careful upgrades/backups

alternatives.name: Excalidraw
alternatives.desc: Excellent collaborative flowcharts, wireframes, and loose visual thinking; it does not pretend to be a proper document editor or structured mind mapper.

facts.install: Open the hosted web app/PWA, or deploy the static app and optional collaboration server
facts.dataFormat: Solo drawings are stored in browser storage or explicit .excalidraw JSON files; exports include PNG and SVG; multiplayer room data is end-to-end encrypted and the decryption key is carried in the share URL
facts.gapVsPaid: Excalidraw is excellent for sketches but does not replace Whimsical's structured documents, dedicated mind maps, polished wireframes, and formal flowchart toolkit.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the hosted app; the trade-off appears later because durable workspace organization, centralized team administration, and managed version history are deliberately minimal

notes: A good yes/kinda boundary; I marked yes because the constrained core is reachable.
prompt:
Build me a single-player flowchart tool like Whimsical. Requirements:

- A local web app: Vite + React, shapes rendered as SVG. No backend, runs as a
  static build, fully offline.
- Shapes: rectangle, rounded rectangle, diamond, ellipse, sticky note, text label.
  Drag to move, handles to resize, double-click to edit text inline.
- Connectors attach to shape anchor points, stay attached when shapes move, route
  orthogonally with arrowheads, and can carry a text label.
- Snap-to-grid plus alignment guides while dragging; keyboard support for
  copy/paste, delete, arrow-key nudge, and undo/redo via a history stack.
- A toolbar with the shape palette and 8 preset fill colors. No free-form style
  panel.
- Boards autosave to IndexedDB (via localforage), with JSON import/export; export
  the selection or the whole board as PNG and SVG.
- No accounts, no telemetry, nothing leaves the browser.
- Out of scope: real-time multiplayer, comments, wireframe component kits, and
  mind-map mode. Flowcharts and stickies only.
- README: npm install / npm run dev, plus the keyboard shortcut list.
